task: Let \(\zeta(k_1,\dots,k_r)=\sum_{n_1>\cdots>n_r\ge 1} n_1^{-k_1}\cdots n_r^{-k_r}\) denote the multiple zeta value, and let \(\{2\}^m\) mean a string of \(m\) copies of \(2\) (with \(\{2\}^0\) the empty string, which is omitted from the list of arguments). For every choice of positive integers \(a,b,c\), which identity is guaranteed to hold?

Let $K$ be a totally real number field, let $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_K$ be its ring of integers, and let $n>2$ be an integer. Recall that a root lattice over $\mathcal O$ is a nonzero finitely generated free $\mathcal O$-module $L$ equipped with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $L\times L\to\mathcal O$ that is totally positive definite and is generated by its roots $\Phi(L)=\{x\in L\mid x\cdot x=2\}$. Fix an irreducible root-system type $X_n$ of rank $n$, and write $c(X_n)$ for the scalar invariant attached to that type. What is the strongest correct statement about the existence of an irreducible root lattice over $\mathcal O$ of type $X_n$ under these assumptions?

For each integer \(n\ge 1\), let \(\delta_n\) denote the maximum density of a sphere packing in \(\mathbf{R}^n\), and let \(\delta_n^L\) denote the maximum density of a lattice sphere packing in \(\mathbf{R}^n\) (that is, a sphere packing whose centers form a lattice). Which of the following is the strongest statement of the form “there exists a constant such that for all integers \(n\ge 1\)” describing their uniform relationship?

Let \(d_1,d_2,d_3>1\) be positive integers such that any repeated value among \(d_1,d_2,d_3\) is odd. Let
\[
R=F_{\mathbb{Q}}[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(x_1^2,x_2^2,x_3^2),\qquad |x_i|=d_i,
\]
where \(F_{\mathbb{Q}}[x_1,x_2,x_3]\) denotes the free graded-commutative \(\mathbb{Q}\)-algebra on homogeneous generators \(x_1,x_2,x_3\). Thus \(R\) is the cohomology algebra of a product of three positive-dimensional spheres over \(\mathbb{Q}\). If \(A\) is an order in \(R\), meaning that \(A\) is a graded subring of \(R\) whose underlying additive group is a graded lattice in \(R\) (equivalently, it is generated by a homogeneous basis of the \(\mathbb{Q}\)-vector space \(R\)), what is the strongest statement that can be proved about the existence of a CW-complex realizing \(A\) in integral cohomology?

Let \(\mathsf H\subsetneq \mathsf G\) be compact connected semisimple Lie groups with \(\mathsf G/\mathsf H\) simply connected and almost effective. Let \(\mathsf A\) be a maximal torus in \(\N_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf H)/\mathsf H\), with \(\dim \mathsf A\ge 2\), and fix \(0<\ell<\dim \mathsf A\). For each \(i\in\mathbb N\), let \(\tilde A_i\subset \mathsf A\) be a compactly embedded subtorus of dimension \(\dim\mathsf A-\ell\), so that \(M_i^n=\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i\) is a homogeneous \(\ell\)-torus bundle. Assume each \((\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i,g_i)\) is a \(\mathsf G\)-homogeneous Einstein torus bundle of submersion type, meaning that any \(\mathsf G\)-invariant metric is also right \(\mathsf A\)-invariant, and that all metrics have Einstein constant \(1\). Convergence in the Grassmannian topology means convergence of the defining subtori \(\tilde A_i\) in the Grassmannian parameterizing such subtori. What is the strongest compactness statement that holds for such a sequence?

Let $K$ be a global function field of characteristic $p>0$, let $K^p\subseteq K$ denote the subfield of $p$th powers, and write $\mathbf A_K$ for the ring of adeles of $K$. Let $(X,\mathcal A)$ be a smooth projective variety with an ample line bundle over $K$, and assume that $(X,\mathcal A)$ descends to $(\widetilde X,\widetilde{\mathcal A})$ over $K^p$. Suppose either
(a) $H^1(X,\mathcal A^{-1})\neq 0$ and $\mathcal A^{\otimes p^{n(\mathcal A)}}$ is globally generated, or
(b) $H^0(X,B_X^1\otimes \mathcal A^{-1})\neq 0$, where $B_X^1$ is the sheaf of locally exact differentials on $X$, and $\mathcal A^{\otimes p}$ is globally generated.
Set $m=p^{n(\mathcal A)}$ in case (a) and $m=p$ in case (b). Let $Y$ be the quotient of the corresponding foliation $\ker(\widetilde{\mathcal A}^{\otimes m})$ on $\widetilde X$, let $\phi:Y\to X$ be the resulting purely inseparable morphism, and let $\psi_{\mathcal A^{\otimes m}}:X\to \mathbb P^N_K$ be the morphism induced by $\mathcal A^{\otimes m}$. If $(x_v)\in X(\mathbf A_K)^{\mathrm{Br}(X)[p]}$ does not lie in the image of $Y(\mathbf A_K)\to X(\mathbf A_K)$, where $X(\mathbf A_K)^{\mathrm{Br}(X)[p]}$ denotes the adelic points orthogonal to the $p$-torsion subgroup of $\mathrm{Br}(X)$, which strongest conclusion follows?

Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, let $N\ge 1$, let $\delta\ge 1$ be an integer that is $\ell^N$-th-power-free, and let $r,s,t>0$ satisfy $r+s+t=\ell^N$. Let $\phi_{\delta}^{(N)}$ denote the CM abelian variety under consideration. Let $\epsilon'_N\in\mu_{\ell-1}(\mathbf{Q}_{\ell})$ (the group of $(\ell-1)$st roots of unity in $\mathbf{Q}_{\ell}$), $b'_N\in\mathbf{Z}$, and $c'_N\in \ell\mathbf{Z}_{\ell}$ satisfy
$$r^r s^s (\ell^N-t)^t\delta^{r+s}=\epsilon'_N\ell^{b'_N}(1+c'_N),$$
and put
$$w=\min\{\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(b'_N),\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(c'_N)\},$$
where $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}$ is the $\ell$-adic valuation. Which description gives the complete factor-by-factor classification of the global root number $W(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})=\prod_{p\le \infty}W_p(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})$ into local terms $W_p(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})$, with the product taken over all finite primes $p$ and the archimedean place $p=\infty$?

Let d>0 be fixed and let p>\frac{2d}{1+2d}. For all sufficiently large n for which a dn-regular graph exists, let G_d be a dn-regular graph on n vertices, and let G(n,p) denote the binomial random graph on the same vertex set, where each edge is included independently with probability p. Write G=G_d\cup G(n,p). A triangle packing in G means a collection of edge-disjoint triangles of G. Which statement is the strongest existence claim that holds in this setting, with high probability (that is, with probability tending to 1 as n\to\infty)?

Let \(n\ge 2\), let \(F_n\) denote a free group of rank \(n\), and let \(F_2\) denote a free group of rank \(2\). For homomorphisms \(g,h:F_n\to F_2\), define their equalizer by
\[
\operatorname{Eq}(g,h)=\{x\in F_n: g(x)=h(x)\},
\]
and write \(\operatorname{rk}(G)\) for the rank of a free group \(G\). (Here, a monomorphism means an injective homomorphism.) Which of the following is the strongest valid existence statement in this setting?

Let $I$ be a stable roommates (SR) instance on $2n$ agents, and let $k$ denote the minimum crossing distance of $I$ (the paper’s structural-distance parameter measuring how far $I$ is from a stable marriage instance). Which of the following is the strongest asymptotic running-time guarantee for computing an optimal stable matching for $I$ as a function of $n$ and $k$?

Let $K$ be a genus-one knot with Seifert matrix $M=\begin{pmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} \end{pmatrix}$ in the canonical band basis (the standard basis coming from the two bands of a genus-one Seifert surface), and for a nonzero integer $\ell$ let $K(\ell,0)$ denote the knot obtained by adding $2\ell$ twists to the first band. Here, $K$ and $K(\ell,0)$ are called $S$-equivalent if they admit Seifert matrices related by the usual $S$-equivalence on Seifert matrices (generated by integral unimodular congruence and elementary expansions/reductions). Which description gives the complete classification of when $K$ and $K(\ell,0)$ are $S$-equivalent?

Fix an integer $k\ge 2$. Let $S_{2k}$ be the space of holomorphic cusp forms of weight $2k$ and level $1$, and let $B_{2k}$ be an orthogonal basis of Hecke eigenforms normalized by
\[
f(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_f(n)\, n^{\frac{2k-1}{2}} e^{2\pi i n z},\qquad a_f(1)=1.
\]
For such $f$, define
\[
A_f(1,n)=\sum_{d^2\mid n} a_f\bigl((n/d^2)^2\bigr).
\]
For a Schwartz function $g\in \mathcal S(0,\infty)$, with Mellin transform $\widetilde g(s)=\int_0^\infty g(x)x^{s-1}\,dx$, and an integer $\ell\ge 1$, set
\[
I_\ell(g)=\sideset{}{^h}\sum_{f\in B_{2k}} a_f(\ell)\sum_{n=1}^\infty A_f(1,n)g(n),
\]
where $\sideset{}{^h}\sum$ denotes the sum weighted by the reciprocal of the Petersson norm. Let $\mu=(1-2k,2k-1,0)$, and define the transform $\mathcal T_\mu$ by
\[
(\mathcal T_\mu g)(y)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{(\sigma)} \widetilde g(1-s)\,\mathcal G_\mu(s)\,y^{-s}\,ds,\qquad \sigma>0.
\]
For an integer $\ell\ge 1$, which strongest identity holds for the associated quantity $I_\ell(g)$?

Let \(\mathcal C\) be a block-stable class of connected graphs, and let \(\mathcal B\) be the class of its 2-connected components (blocks). Write \(B(y)\) for the exponential generating function of \(\mathcal B\), let \(\rho_B\) be the radius of convergence of \(B\), and define
\[
u_C:=\frac{1}{\rho_B B''(\rho_B)}.
\]
Let \(C^{\bullet}(x,u)\) be the exponential generating function of connected rooted graphs in \(\mathcal C\), where \(x\) marks vertices and \(u\) marks blocks. For fixed \(u>0\), let \(\mathbb P_\nu\) denote the fixed-size block-weighted law under which a rooted graph \(G\in\mathcal C^{\bullet}\) with \(n\) vertices is sampled with probability proportional to \(u^{b(G)}\), where \(b(G)\) is the number of blocks of \(G\). The block tree of a sampled graph is the tree recording how its blocks are attached. Which statement holds for every such class \(\mathcal C\)?

Let \(U\) denote the unknot, and let \(\rho_p(K)\) denote the scale-invariant \(p\)-density associated to a knot type \(K\) in \(\mathbb{R}^3\), for each parameter \(p\in(-1,\infty]\). What is the strongest statement that holds for every knot type \(K\) and every \(p\in(-1,\infty]\)?

For integers \(n\ge 1\) and \(0\le m<n\), write \(H(n,m)^{\mathrm{ab}}\) for the abelianization of the group \(H(n,m)\). Which of the following statements is equivalent to \(H(n,m)^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong \mathbb{Z}^2\)?

Let $L(\lambda)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathfrak{spo}(4|1)$ with highest weight $\lambda=m_1\omega_1+2m_2\omega_2$, where $m_1,m_2\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ and $\omega_1,\omega_2$ are the fundamental weights; when referring to shape, view $\lambda$ as the partition $(m_1+m_2,m_2)$. Let $v_\lambda$ be a highest weight vector, and let $f_1,f_2$ be the root vectors corresponding to the negative simple roots. Define the set of Verma vectors
\[
H:= \left\{ f_1^{b_4} f_2^{b_3} f_1^{b_2} f_2^{b_1} v_\lambda \,\middle|\,
\begin{aligned}
&b_i\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\ (i=1,2,3,4),\\
&0\le b_1\le 2m_2,\\
&0\le b_2\le m_1+b_1,\\
&0\le b_3\le \min\{b_2+m_1,\,2b_2\},\\
&0\le b_4\le \min\{m_1,\,\tfrac12 b_3\}
\end{aligned}
\right\}.
\]
Which objects are in weight-preserving one-to-one correspondence with the elements of $H$?

Let \(\mathbb R_+\) denote the positive real numbers. Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq \mathbb R^n\) be a nondegenerate submanifold, and let \(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n:\mathbb R_+\to(0,1)\) be non-increasing functions. A point \(x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb R^n\) is called \((\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n)\)-approximable if there exist infinitely many integers \(q\ge 1\) and integers \(p_1,\dots,p_n\) such that \(|qx_i-p_i|<\psi_i(q)\) for every \(i\). Which statement gives the correct criterion, in terms of \(\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\cdots \psi_n(q)\), for whether almost all points of \(\mathcal M\) (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure on \(\mathcal M\)) are \((\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n)\)-approximable?

Let \(k(n)\) denote the kissing number in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), i.e. the maximum number of nonoverlapping unit spheres that can simultaneously be tangent to a central unit sphere in \(n\)-dimensional Euclidean space. Which of the following is the strongest quantitative estimate that holds for \(k(19)\)?

Fix an integer \(n\ge 3\). Let \(\mathbb B^n\subset \mathbb R^n\) be the unit ball, let \(\mathrm{Sym}_n\) denote the real symmetric \(n\times n\) matrices, and write \(L^\infty(\mathbb B^n,\mathrm{Sym}_n)\) for essentially bounded measurable \(\mathrm{Sym}_n\)-valued matrix fields. A function \(u\) is positively \(\alpha\)-homogeneous if \(u(tx)=t^\alpha u(x)\) whenever \(t>0\) and \(x,tx\in \mathbb B^n\). Which of the following is the strongest valid statement asserting the existence of uniformly elliptic measurable coefficients and homogeneous weak solutions of a divergence-form equation in \(\mathbb B^n\), with explicit dependence on a parameter \(\gamma\ge 1\)?

Let \(H(y,p)=\tfrac12|p|^2+V(y)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(V\in \mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{R}^n)\) is \(\mathbb{Z}^n\)-periodic, and let \(g\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)\). For each \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(u^\varepsilon\in C(\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty))\) be the viscosity solution of
\[
\begin{cases}
 u_t^\varepsilon+\tfrac12|Du^\varepsilon|^2+V(x/\varepsilon)=\tfrac\varepsilon2\,\Delta u^\varepsilon & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty),\\
 u^\varepsilon(x,0)=g(x) & \text{on }\mathbb{R}^n,
\end{cases}
\]
and let \(u\in C(\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty))\) be the viscosity solution of the homogenized problem
\[
\begin{cases}
 u_t+\overline H(Du)=0 & \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty),\\
 u(x,0)=g(x) & \text{on }\mathbb{R}^n,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\overline H\) is the effective Hamiltonian associated with \(H\). What is the strongest uniform quantitative estimate on \(|u^\varepsilon(x,t)-u(x,t)|\) that holds for all \((x,t)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times[0,\infty)\) and all \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\)?
